claims.statement: The create-file fragment describes Add file then Create new file, or the left file-tree plus icon. The caption was read but screenshot not visually inspected. UI entry points are not write permission, approved content, an actual file creation, or committed change evidence.

The email selector appears only in fpt/ghec and describes choosing among verified addresses when multiple account addresses exist, with a no-reply default when privacy is enabled. It establishes neither an actual account address nor cryptographic authorship; the screenshot and linked address-format guide were not reviewed as evidence of this user's identity.

The branch fragment offers current/new branch selection and recommends a new branch plus pull request when editing the default branch. This should-level upstream advice is not a mandatory adopted policy, actual branch protection, review approval, or proof that a PR was opened; the image was not visually inspected.

The two-step fragment describes creating a proposed-change PR and selecting a desired PR from its list. Selection does not merge the PR, establish approval, passing checks, merge permission, or verified release; no PR was created or merged from these instructions.

The fpt/ghec email-options fragment distinguishes choosing verified author addresses for UI edit/delete/create/merge when privacy is off from fixed no-reply authorship when privacy is on. It adds a stronger cannot-change condition than the default-only wording in the selector fragment; the combined source scope is preserved without claiming an actual privacy setting, signature verification, or access to personal account data.

The commit-message fragment recommends a short meaningful description and permits multiple-author attribution in the message, linking to coauthor guidance. Descriptive attribution is not identity verification, consent, signed authorship, actual review, or evidence of a completed commit; the linked guide is not reviewed by this receipt.
